runtime.activation.trigger: when deciding whether PactKit phase rules apply
skip_when: no PactKit workflow is invoked or requested
evidence: the user explicitly invoked or requested the workflow
runtime.activation.override: the user's latest explicit workflow choice controls activation

skip_when: the user requests another supported execution model
evidence: work continues in the current host session unless the user chooses otherwise
runtime.current-session.override: the user may explicitly request another supported execution model

evidence: output matches the user's language
runtime.language.override: the user may request another language

evidence: the evidence input fingerprint still matches current inputs
runtime.evidence-reuse.override: rerun when freshness is uncertain or the user requests it

safety.credentials.trigger: before exposing or persisting a secret
skip_when: the content is verified non-secret test data
evidence: no credential or secret is disclosed or committed

safety.authorization.trigger: before an external side effect such as push, PR, publish, release, or message
skip_when: the action is read-only or confined to the authorized local workspace
evidence: current user authorization covers the exact action and target

safety.irreversible-damage.trigger: before a destructive or materially irreversible operation
skip_when: the operation is read-only or safely reversible
evidence: the exact target is resolved and recovery or authorization is established
safety.irreversible-damage.override: explicit authorization cannot override platform safety

invariants: preserve existing project and user files

project-plan.entry: explicit planning request for one bounded change
invariants: requirements are testable and scope is explicit
the Spec never instructs the implementer to amend it during Act (findings land in the commit message or a docs/ note)

project-clarify.entry: explicit clarification request or material ambiguity
invariants: unanswered questions remain visible and never become invented facts

project-act.entry: explicit implementation request with a usable objective
invariants: scope integrity
edit the source of truth
safe work remains available
guidance gaps are closed by need, not by a fixed read count
review is read-only unless the user also requests repair
verification setup matches the Spec's actor and environment
test environment provenance is confirmed (running code == code under test)
a defect finding sweeps its class — same-pattern sites are checked before a pass verdict
user-path validation is distinguished from Spec-conformance verification — key scenarios run through the real end-user path, not a privileged one
reuse and not-applicable claims are checked independently of the load trace
completion_evidence: security, quality, test adequacy, freshness, and Spec alignment assessed

project-done.entry: explicit finalization request for verified work
invariants: reuse fresh evidence and disclose every remaining gap
no engineering-guide selection overrides a verification decision's meaning
completion_evidence: required verification is adequate for the Spec's actor and environment, and current

invariants: publishing requires exact current authorization
push and PR creation require exact current authorization
completion_evidence: summary, risk, and test evidence are complete

invariants: escalate when product behavior or architecture expands

project-design.entry: explicit greenfield or multi-story product design request
invariants: outcomes and non-goals remain explicit
completion_evidence: scope, risks, and dependencies are traceable

project-sprint.entry: explicit request to execute an ordered PDCA sequence
invariants: exactly one phase capsule is active at a time
completion_evidence: each entered phase meets its own completion evidence

invariants: test hypotheses against evidence before proposing a cause

concurrency.md.trigger: Concurrent execution or shared mutable state is in scope.
questions: Is work I/O-bound or CPU-bound?
Who owns ordering and cancellation?
safe_invariants: Bound workers and queues.
Synchronize shared mutable state and expose failures.
defaults: Reuse the project executor with configurable limits.
alternatives: Use sequential execution when load does not justify concurrency.
evidence: Contention, ordering, cancellation, and shutdown tests.
non_applicable: Single-threaded work with no shared state or parallel execution.

async-patterns.md.trigger: An async boundary or event loop is changed.
questions: Which calls can block?
How are timeout and cancellation propagated?
safe_invariants: Do not block an event loop.
Close resources on success, failure, and cancellation.
defaults: Keep a coherent async model and bound external waits.
alternatives: Use synchronous code when concurrency needs are small or dependencies are synchronous.
evidence: Timeout, cancellation, cleanup, and concurrent-call tests.
non_applicable: Pure synchronous code with no async callers or resources.

configuration.md.trigger: Runtime configuration, environment values, or secrets change.
questions: Which values vary by environment?
What is required and what has a safe default?
safe_invariants: Never persist credentials in source or public artifacts.
Validate untrusted configuration.
defaults: Use existing config layering and fail clearly for missing required values.
alternatives: Use a named code constant for a true invariant.
evidence: Precedence, invalid-input, missing-value, and redaction tests.
non_applicable: A local detail that cannot vary by deployment.

observability.md.trigger: A runtime path needs operational diagnosis or service-level signals.
questions: Which failures must operators distinguish?
Which identifiers safely correlate events?
safe_invariants: Do not log credentials or sensitive payloads.
Telemetry must not fail the primary operation.
defaults: Reuse project logging and record structured outcomes and correlation fields.
alternatives: Metrics or traces may answer the operational question better than logs.
evidence: Captured failure signals and sensitive-field redaction evidence.
non_applicable: Pure library logic already observable through its caller.

module-design.md.trigger: Responsibilities, boundaries, or public interfaces are added or moved.
questions: Who owns this responsibility?
Can callers use a smaller stable interface?
safe_invariants: Avoid circular ownership and parallel sources of truth.
defaults: Follow an existing boundary and extract cohesive, independently testable behavior.
alternatives: Local duplication can be clearer than premature abstraction.
evidence: Caller map, public-interface tests, and ownership rationale.
non_applicable: A contained change inside an established boundary.

database.md.trigger: Persistent database reads, writes, schema, or transactions change.
questions: What consistency and isolation are required?
What is the query and transaction cost?
safe_invariants: Parameterize untrusted values.
Release connections and preserve atomicity on failure.
defaults: Reuse the project pool and keep transactions scoped to database work.
alternatives: Choose optimistic locking, atomic updates, or serialization from contention evidence.
evidence: Query-plan or index evidence plus rollback, conflict, and failure tests.
non_applicable: No persistent database interaction or schema impact.

caching.md.trigger: A cache is introduced or its lifecycle changes.
questions: What is the source of truth?
How are invalidation, bounds, and stale reads handled?
safe_invariants: A cache cannot be an undeclared source of truth.
Bound memory growth.
defaults: Prefer cache-aside with explicit invalidation and measured usefulness.
alternatives: Use immutable keys, explicit versions, or no cache when safer than TTL.
evidence: Hit/miss, invalidation, expiry, stampede, and capacity evidence.
non_applicable: No repeated expensive read or measured latency need.

api-integration.md.trigger: An external HTTP, RPC, webhook, or service contract changes.
questions: What are timeout, retry, schema, and ownership boundaries?
Is the operation idempotent?
safe_invariants: Validate untrusted responses.
Do not retry non-idempotent actions without deduplication.
defaults: Reuse the project client with bounded timeout and typed validation.
alternatives: Fail fast, queue, cache, or degrade according to consistency needs.
evidence: Contract, timeout, partial-response, retry, and duplicate-delivery tests.
non_applicable: No call crosses a process or trust boundary.

event-driven.md.trigger: Events, queues, subscribers, or at-least-once delivery are introduced.
questions: What are delivery and ordering guarantees?
How are duplicates handled?
safe_invariants: Make retried handlers safe and failed delivery observable.
defaults: Use versioned schemas, stable event IDs, and bounded retry or dead-letter handling.
alternatives: Use a synchronous call when the caller requires the result immediately.
evidence: Duplicate, ordering, schema-version, and dead-letter tests.
non_applicable: No asynchronous message boundary or downstream fan-out.

resilience.md.trigger: A remote dependency or overload-sensitive runtime path can fail.
questions: Which failures are transient?
What is the resource and latency budget?
safe_invariants: Bound waits, retries, queues, and resources.
Do not hide permanent failure as success.
defaults: Use explicit timeout and limited retry for recoverable operations.
alternatives: Choose circuit breaking, bulkheads, backpressure, or immediate failure from evidence.
evidence: Timeout, overload, dependency outage, and recovery tests.
non_applicable: Pure in-process deterministic logic without resource contention.

memory-management.md.trigger: Data volume, lifetime, caching, streaming, or resource ownership changes.
questions: What bounds allocation?
Who releases long-lived references?
safe_invariants: Bound collections fed by untrusted input.
Release owned resources on every path.
defaults: Stream unknown-size inputs and use context-managed resources.
alternatives: Materialize inputs when a verified small bound improves clarity.
evidence: Peak-memory, large-input, cleanup, and repeated-operation evidence.
non_applicable: Small fixed-size values with no retained resources.

code-review-first.md.trigger: The project contains nearby patterns or abstractions.
questions: What is the closest maintained exemplar?
Why does redundant-looking code exist?
safe_invariants: Do not bypass security or ownership abstractions without evidence.
defaults: Follow project conventions and inspect history when intent is unclear.
alternatives: Introduce a new pattern when existing ones cannot meet a documented requirement.
evidence: Exemplar, caller/history inspection, and capability-gap rationale.
non_applicable: Greenfield code with no meaningful project precedent.

component-reuse.md.trigger: A capability may exist in the project, framework, or ecosystem.
questions: Can an existing public interface meet the need?
What is the trust and maintenance cost?
safe_invariants: Do not implement cryptographic or authentication primitives ad hoc.
defaults: Evaluate standard library, project abstraction, then framework capability.
alternatives: Prefer small local code over a dependency when behavior is well bounded.
evidence: Capability comparison, reuse decision, and compatibility tests.
non_applicable: The requirement is novel and no comparable capability exists.

error-recovery.md.trigger: Partial failure, retry, resumability, or interrupted writes are possible.
questions: Is failure transient?
Can retry duplicate or corrupt the operation?
safe_invariants: Bound retries and preserve failure context.
Do not silently discard partial failure.
defaults: Fail fast for permanent errors; retry idempotent transient errors with bounded backoff.
alternatives: Resume, compensate, quarantine, or manual recovery may fit better than retry.
evidence: Interrupted-run, duplicate-attempt, terminal-error, and recovery tests.
non_applicable: Atomic deterministic work with no recoverable intermediate state.

data-consistency.md.trigger: One logical change spans records, stores, services, or concurrent writers.
questions: What consistency level is required?
What compensation or conflict policy applies?
safe_invariants: Do not claim unavailable atomicity.
Protect against lost updates.
defaults: Use the smallest transaction boundary satisfying the invariant.
alternatives: Saga, outbox, optimistic concurrency, or eventual consistency require explicit trade-offs.
evidence: Conflict, duplicate, compensation, and partial-commit tests.
non_applicable: A single atomic write with no concurrent or distributed boundary.

backwards-compatibility.md.trigger: A public API, CLI, config, schema, protocol, or layout changes.
questions: Which old callers or data must work?
What are migration and rollback semantics?
safe_invariants: Do not execute irreversible high-risk migration without exact authorization.
defaults: Add before remove, preserve declared aliases, and make migration idempotent.
alternatives: Use a versioned break or explicit rejection when compatibility is impossible.
evidence: Legacy fixture, repeated upgrade, interrupted migration, and rollback evidence.
non_applicable: Private implementation with no persisted or externally consumed shape.

performance-antipatterns.md.trigger: A hot path, large collection, query fan-out, or latency target changes.
questions: What measured budget is at risk?
Does work scale with input or caller count?
safe_invariants: Bound untrusted work and avoid unbounded query or allocation growth.
defaults: Measure first; batch, paginate, or index the proven bottleneck.
alternatives: Prefer clear simple code when evidence shows no material risk.
evidence: Representative benchmark, query count, complexity, or profile evidence.
non_applicable: Cold or fixed-size path with no performance requirement.

graceful-shutdown.md.trigger: A service, worker, pool, or background task owns resources.
questions: How are new and in-flight work sequenced?
What is the shutdown deadline?
safe_invariants: Do not abandon durable state or leave owned resources running.
defaults: Stop intake, drain within a bound, close dependencies, and expose timeout failure.
alternatives: Immediate termination can fit stateless disposable work.
evidence: Signal, drain, timeout, forced-stop, and cleanup tests.
non_applicable: Short-lived commands without background work or persistent resources.

testing-strategy.md.trigger: Behavior, regression coverage, or trust boundaries materially change.
questions: Would the test fail if implementation were removed?
Which boundary and failure paths matter?
safe_invariants: Tests cannot expose credentials or mutate uncontrolled external systems.
defaults: Assert observable behavior and reproduce the defect before relying on mocks.
alternatives: Select unit, integration, contract, property, mutation, or E2E depth from risk.
evidence: Behavior assertion, defect reproduction, boundary cases, and negative control.
non_applicable: Generated or documentation-only change with deterministic structural validation.

operational-readiness.md.trigger: A service, scheduled task, worker, or rollout behavior changes.
questions: How will operators detect failure?
What rollout, capacity, and rollback signals exist?
safe_invariants: Do not expose sensitive diagnostics or report false readiness.
defaults: Define health signals, failure visibility, capacity bounds, and rollback criteria.
alternatives: Use a flag, canary, shadow run, or manual rollback according to deployment risk.
evidence: Isolated deploy, startup/shutdown, degraded dependency, and rollback evidence.
non_applicable: Non-running library, docs, or build-time-only code.

dependency-supply-chain.md.trigger: A dependency, package source, lockfile, or installer changes.
questions: Is it necessary?
What source, license, scripts, binaries, and permissions are introduced?
safe_invariants: Do not execute untrusted scripts or expand privileges without review.
defaults: Pin reproducibly, retain integrity metadata, and prefer maintained minimal dependencies.
alternatives: Use the standard library, an existing dependency, vendoring, or bounded local code.
evidence: Dependency diff, provenance, license, advisory, script, and clean-install evidence.
non_applicable: No dependency graph, source, binary, installer, or permission change.

ui-state-accessibility.md.trigger: Interactive UI structure, state, or navigation changes.
questions: What are loading, empty, error, disabled, and optimistic states?
Can keyboard and assistive users complete the task?
safe_invariants: Preserve keyboard access, visible focus, semantic labels, and error recovery.
defaults: Use semantic controls, managed focus, labelled states, responsive overflow, and rollback.
alternatives: Use platform-native interactions instead of custom behavior when suitable.
evidence: Keyboard, focus, label, contrast, state, and responsive tests.
non_applicable: No user interface, rendered state, or interaction behavior changes.

write-safety.md.trigger: Writing to a file that already exists and may contain content the writer did not generate (configs, user tool files, managed sections).
questions: Who owns each section of this file — the writer, the user, or another tool?
Litmus test: does this file contain content I did not generate?
safe_invariants: MUST NOT fully replace a file with mixed ownership — full replacement silently destroys content the writer did not generate.
One authoritative location per truth; every duplicate drifts (no dual-write)
defaults: Generator owns 100% of the file → full replace is safe; mixed ownership → incremental merge (Edit/patch/append, or only the writer-owned section); unsure → merge
alternatives: Write a candidate (.new) and let the human accept — the deployer's ownership-manifest pattern
evidence: A merge-or-replace decision recorded for each pre-existing file written, and zero full replaces on mixed-ownership files
non_applicable: Files created fresh by this change — no prior content to destroy.
